In Justin McDonald’s “Building character through dead copywriters and marketing legends,” the imagined round table includes direct-mail copywriter Gary Halbert, author Dale Carnegie, Napoleon Hill, advertising copywriter Eugene Schwartz, and references to Brian Kurtz, Dan Kennedy, and Charles Darwin. Justin McDonald’s piece presents character-building and success as supported by self-suggestion, persistence, organized effort, patience, focus, self-confidence, a sense of justice and humor, understanding of humanity, and the ability to tolerate others. It suggests that studying the work and life stories of successful writers and entrepreneurs can provide guidance.

Justin McDonald’s writing style in “Building character through dead copywriters and marketing legends” is conversational, humorous, highly descriptive, introspective, and deliberately digressive. It uses first-person narration, rhetorical questions, colloquial asides, playful exaggeration, and dreamlike imagery, including the scroll, candlelit reading, chamomile tea, and a fantastical round-table gathering.

In writing discussed on 2022-11-03, Justin McDonald argues that entrepreneurs should consider outsourcing or delegating tasks they cannot do exceptionally well. He distinguishes outsourcing—having another person or company perform work—from passing the buck, which he describes as handing off a situation blindly and merely hoping it gets done. He recalls that outsourcing helped a small print shop where he worked succeed and concludes that delegated work need not be done exactly the owner’s way if it achieves the same result: “good enough is good enough.”
